content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies information bottleneck as a way to train adversarially robust neural network. Unlike previous method, this paper utilize the causal theory to analyze the reason why deep neural network suffers from adversarial attack. The proposed method, called CausalIB train the network by information bottleneck compounded with a causal loss.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Overall this paper is clear in most parts and the idea of combining IB with causal loss is new to me. I am glad to see the authors considered the possibility of gradient obfuscation issue.

However, the weaknesses of this paper are also significant:
1. Details lacking: a couple of crucial details are missing in this paper. Specifically, how the models are trained under the new loss function; how the causal loss || w_xyi - w_xyj || is implemented (readers are confused how w_xy is estimated). 
2. Authors mentioned that this training method is slow so no bigger network or datasets can be tested. But we don’t know the actual running time complexity. Would be great to mention in the paper.
3. Table-1: why highlight CausalIB if AT is better?
4. How \alpha and \beta are chosen in the experiments? Also, it would be better to check cases where \beta=0 and see if causal loss really plays a role.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity and reproducibility of this paper are questionable given the reasons above. Also given that this paper is a combination of IB and causal loss, I am a bit unsure how novel it is compared with other papers.
content.summary_of_the_review: I tend to reject currently, due to the reasons I listed above. Authors need to improve the clarity and add more implementation details in the next revision.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces causal inference to the information bottleneck method and disentangles robust features and non-robust features to further improve the robustness of IB framework.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[Strength]
1. The paper tries to address the robustness problem from the perspective of causal inference, which makes sense to some extent.
2. The experimental results are promising.

[Weakness]
1. This paper seems to be a simple A+B work, and it just simply introduces the existing method of improving robustness through Causal Intervention in paper [Adversarial Visual Robustness by Causal Intervention] rooted in the Information Bottleneck framework.
2. This paper even misunderstands some basic concepts in Causal Intervention. The paper states "then the robust feature w_{xy} can be learned by Eq. 7:", but w_{xy} is not a feature at all. It is the weight of the mapping from x to y. In the paper [Adversarial Visual Robustness by Causal Intervention], it is mentioned that "all variables are assumed to be linked by linear weights w∗". 
3. Many methods similar to this paper have already been proposed, which add noise to the feature layer to achieve the intervention. Although those papers are not explained in terms of causal interventions. E.g., [Boosting Adversarial Robustness using Feature Level Stochastic Smoothing], [Simple and Effective Stochastic Neural Networks]
4.The motivation of the paper is not clear. The paper mentions this work because of the IB method "which leads to the limitation of its further improvement of adversarial robustness". This statement is too general, as almost all the deep learning methods can be described as being designed to improve performance, which is not a clear motivation at all.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality of the paper is low, with unclear motivation and limited novelty.
content.summary_of_the_review: I judged the papers on the quality of the writing, the novelty of the approach, the clarity of the motivation and the feasibility of the method.

content.title: Response to Official Review of Paper1077 by Reviewer z5Rm
content.comment:
1. The information bottleneck method aims at solving the problems in the field of representation learning. Therefore, causality rather than correlation should be considered under such a scenario. It is not a simple A+B work. Actually, since few work in the information bottleneck considers the scenario of causality, our research motivation is clear.
2. The causal graph we provide is based on the assumption that the model is linear, and the application of our causal graph and instrumental variables is also built on such an assumption. Thus, the causal effect can also be simulated by the formula under the linear model, and the feature learned under the linear model is the weight that points from $X$ to $Y$ .
3. The model structure used in the paper the reviewer mentioned is utilized in multiple studies, especially in the research which is related to Variational Autoencoders. Due to the similarity to some extent between variational inference and information bottleneck theory, the method we have adopted to implement information bottleneck theory is based on the network structure of variational autoencoders. Thus, rather than our network being similar to the network used in the paper the reviewer mentioned, the paper is very similar to the variational autoencoder structure,or more precisely, the structure of all the networks related to Variational Autoencoders are very similar. Although the methods are similar,  the problem to be resolved is different that our method introduces a new causal technique in the information bottelneck framework.
4. Our motivation is to incorporate the causality into the IB method to learn robust features. We agree that the insight should not be focuses on the performance. We appreciate the review comment and would refine the manuscript.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors proposed a method to improve the robustness of the deep neural network (DNN) against adversarial attacks. The method utilized the causal theory and the information bottleneck (IB) framework to disentangle the robust features and non-robust features. This helps DNN to focus more on the content features and suppresses the influence of non-robust features. The authors also provided extensive experiments and sanity checks of the gradient obfuscation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1. The authors combined the IB framework and causal theory to improve the robustness of DNN. They also brought out the reasons for incorporating causal theory and provided experiments to justify the effectiveness of their method. 

2. The authors carried out the sanity check of gradient obfuscation for their method, which is great since some defense methods fall into the pitfall of this issue.

Weaknesses:

1. The authors claim that the generation process of an image can be formulated by the causal graph. Is it possible that a different dataset will exist a different corresponding causal graph? How do we verify the graph given a dataset? Is there any simulation or toy example to show?

2. The defense model this method compared to should include other mixup methods, such as manifold mixup, and align mixup since they manipulate in the feature layer (the concept layer) instead of the image layer. The original mixup only works on the image layer.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
[Clarity]

There are a few things that can be improved.

1. Formula (1), the loss function of IB, and in the next two sentences, the authors used I(Z; Y) and I(Z; X) in the formula. However, in formulas (2), (3), and the sentence above formula (2), the authors used I(Z, Y) and I(Z, X). Not sure if those are typos.

2. In the causal graph in Figures 2 and 3, the authors can strengthen and enlarge arrows in order to help the reader to see easily where the arrows point to.

3. Maybe a few lines to explain how to formulate equation (10) for readers who are not familiar with causal inference.

[Quality]

Good quality in the paper writing and presentation of experiments.

[Novelty]

The combination of IB and causal theory is new to me, and using causal theory to separate robust and non-robust features is interesting.

[Reproducibility]

Not sure, I haven't seen the code yet.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper addressed the robustness issue through two theories: information bottleneck and causal theory. Even if some concepts in their design aren't new, the authors did combine them into a somewhat novel method and provided reasons and experiments to justify their method. I believed this is an above-average paper.
